dedupe_keys.name: social cost benefit analysis of rehabilitating multipurpose small reservoirs in northern ghana ecosystem services 2021

description: This case study is an economic appraisal of rehabilitating multipurpose small reservoirs in northern Ghana, published in Ecosystem Services in 2021 by Bekoe, Balana and Nimoh. The reservoirs supply irrigation and other uses in a water-stressed area, but the ecosystem services they provide have declined for years because of missing rehabilitation and poor management. Using selected reservoirs and secondary and survey data, the authors run an ecosystem services-based social cost-benefit analysis. Private financial returns from irrigated crops show a negative net present value and an internal rate of return below the cost of capital, so private investors have no incentive to rehabilitate; adding livestock watering, fisheries, recreation, domestic water and climate regulation gives positive NPV and an IRR up to 43 percent. The authors recommend public investment and a public, private and user partnership business model, and warn that policy focused only on irrigation benefits is biased against reservoir development. Coverage: selected reservoirs in one region. Access: free abstract page; the full text and licence were not read. Caveats: the number of reservoirs and valuation methods are in the full paper. It informs investment appraisal of small dams and irrigation infrastructure in economic and optimisation models, and lists no linked catalogue records.
